hornbill: A RHINOCEROS HORNBILL perched on a branch in side profile. Glossy BLACK body and wings, a WHITE BELLY AND THIGH TUFT, and a long WHITE TAIL crossed by ONE BROAD BLACK BAND. Its bill is a large pale creamy-yellow downcurved bill, and rising from the base of that bill is a HUGE SMOOTH ORANGE-RED CASQUE that CURVES UPWARD AND FORWARD like a rhinoceros horn, well clear of the head. Pale eye ringed in red. The upcurved orange-red horn above the bill is the whole point
raccoondog: A raccoon dog, a tanuki: a SHORT-LEGGED STOCKY ROUND-BODIED canid with very thick grizzled brown and grey fur, a small pointed muzzle, SMALL ROUNDED EARS, and a BLACK RACCOON-LIKE FACIAL MASK across both eyes and cheeks with pale fur above the eyes and a white muzzle. Dark legs, and a SHORT THICK BUSHY TAIL with NO RINGS ON IT. A fat fluffy little dog with a bandit mask, not a raccoon and not a fox
kinkajou: A kinkajou clinging to a branch, a small golden-brown rainforest mammal with a ROUNDED TEDDY-BEAR-LIKE HEAD, a short blunt muzzle, small round ears set low on the sides, very large dark eyes, dense woolly honey-gold fur, and a LONG THICK PREHENSILE TAIL curled around the branch. On a completely plain flat uniform light gray backdrop, no white box, no panel, no frame behind it
proboscis: A proboscis monkey sitting on a branch, a large orange-brown monkey with a rounded pot belly, pale grey limbs and a long pale tail. The male has a FLESHY DROOPING NOSE that hangs down over his upper lip - LARGE BUT IN PROPORTION, about the size of his own muzzle, NOT a huge trunk, NOT reaching past his chin. On a completely plain flat uniform light gray backdrop, no white box, no panel, no frame behind it
ayeaye: An aye-aye clinging to a branch, a strange lemur with shaggy black-brown fur, ENORMOUS THIN LEATHERY BAT-LIKE EARS, huge orange staring eyes, prominent rodent-like front teeth, and one extremely long thin skeletal MIDDLE FINGER held out. It has EXACTLY ONE TAIL: a single long bushy tail, one only, no second tail anywhere
tasdevil: A Tasmanian devil standing calmly on all four short legs with its MOUTH CLOSED and a NEUTRAL GENTLE EXPRESSION, not snarling, not gaping, no bared teeth, not aggressive. A squat black dog-sized marsupial with a very large broad head, a thick neck, a white band across the chest, short legs, a stout tail and a small pink nose. Calm and quiet
kudu: A greater kudu bull standing on all four legs, a VERY TALL SLENDER GREY-BROWN ANTELOPE with LONG THIN LEGS, a deep narrow chest, a high shoulder hump, a long neck, and a straight back sloping slightly down to the rump. Six to eight narrow WHITE VERTICAL STRIPES down each flank, a white chevron between the eyes, very large rounded ears, a fringe of hair along the throat, and enormous open SPIRAL CORKSCREW HORNS sweeping up in two or three loose twists. Tall, leggy and deer-like in build
saiga: A saiga antelope standing on all four legs, a pale sandy antelope with a SHORT SWOLLEN DOWNTURNED NOSE - a bulbous puffy muzzle with the nostrils facing DOWNWARD, like a slightly inflated sheep's nose. It is SHORT AND STUBBY, absolutely NOT a long trunk, NOT an elephant snout, NOT reaching below the mouth. Ribbed amber horns, large dark eyes, a stocky body and slim legs
mammoth: A woolly mammoth standing in side profile, an elephantine beast under a long shaggy reddish-brown coat, with a high domed head and a shoulder hump. It has EXACTLY ONE TRUNK, a single trunk hanging from the middle of its face and curling at the tip, and EXACTLY TWO TUSKS, one on each side of the trunk, both long curving spiralling ivory tusks sweeping forward and inward. Two tusks and one trunk, correctly attached to the face, no extra tusks and no second trunk
leopardseal: A leopard seal lying on ice, a long sleek muscular seal with a serpentine reptilian head and a long neck. Its coat is DARK SILVER-GREY ON THE BACK fading to a PALE SILVER-WHITE THROAT AND BELLY, and it is COVERED IN SCATTERED DARK GREY AND BLACK SPOTS, densest along the flanks and across the pale throat, which is what gives it the name leopard. Long fore-flippers, a wide mouth, closed
spermwhale: A sperm whale swimming in side profile, an enormous uniform grey whale whose front third is a MASSIVE BLUNT SQUARE BOX-LIKE HEAD with a flat vertical front, a single blowhole at the top left of the snout, and a NARROW UNDERSLUNG LOWER JAW tucked beneath it lined with small pegs of teeth. Wrinkled prune-like skin along the body, a small rounded dorsal hump rather than a fin, a row of low knuckles behind it, small paddle flippers and a broad triangular fluke
whaleshark: A whale shark swimming, an enormous broad flat-headed shark with a wide terminal mouth across the front of its head. Its dark blue-grey skin carries a REGULAR LATTICE PATTERN of PALE CREAM ROUND SPOTS arranged in neat rows between PALE VERTICAL AND HORIZONTAL STRIPES, like a checkerboard grid of dots and lines across the back and flanks, with prominent ridges running along its sides, a tall crescent tail and small remoras nearby
narwhal: A narwhal swimming in side profile, a stout arctic whale with a rounded blunt forehead, a small mouth, no dorsal fin at all - only a low ridge along the back - and small curled paddle flippers. Its skin is MOTTLED ALL OVER with dense DARK GREY AND BLACK BLOTCHES ON A PALE CREAM-WHITE GROUND, darkest along the back and fading pale beneath. A SINGLE LONG STRAIGHT SPIRALLING IVORY TUSK projects forward from the left side of its upper jaw, twisted like a rope
flyingsquirrel: A flying squirrel gliding, a small squirrel with LOOSE FURRY SKIN - the patagium - stretched between its OUTSTRETCHED FRONT LEG AND HIND LEG ON EACH SIDE, forming a flat furry rectangle of skin edged with fur along the body. The membrane is SKIN JOINING THE LIMBS, absolutely NOT feathered wings, NOT bat wings with finger bones, NOT separate wings growing from the back. Huge round black eyes, a broad flattened bushy tail held out behind
arctichare: An arctic hare sitting in snow, a large PURE WHITE hare drawn with a LIGHT SOFT WARM-GREY OUTLINE and VERY FEW INTERNAL LINES - no dark shading patches, no grey smudges, no dirty markings anywhere on the body. One flat clean white all over with only faint pale grey shadow. Compact rounded body, very short ears with SMALL BLACK TIPS, dark eyes, a small dark nose and large furred hind feet
bat: A fruit bat, a flying fox, in flight with its wings fully spread wide on both sides, seen in three-quarter front view. A fox-like head with a long pointed muzzle, a black nose, large round dark eyes and two upright pointed ears, russet-brown fur, and broad dark brown leathery wing membranes. It has NO TAIL AT ALL - the rear body ends cleanly between the legs with no tail of any kind
rustyspottedcat: A rusty-spotted cat, the smallest wild cat in the world, standing on all four legs, a tiny fine-boned cat with a small rounded head and very large eyes. Its coat is a SOFT EVEN PALE GREY-FAWN marked ONLY with small SOFT RUSTY REDDISH-BROWN BLOTCHES in gentle lengthwise lines - no dark shading patches, no grey smudges, no dirty blotches, no heavy shadow masses anywhere. Clean flat fur colour, two thin dark streaks on each cheek, small rounded ears, a short plain tail
kodkod: A kodkod, or guina, standing on all four legs, a very small house-cat-sized wild cat with a small rounded head, short blunt muzzle, small round ears and large eyes, warm ochre-brown fur covered in small dense round black spots, and dark cheek streaks. It has EXACTLY ONE TAIL: a single thick bushy tail ringed with dark bands, one tail only, no second tail anywhere
dikdik: A dik-dik standing on all four legs, THE SMALLEST ANTELOPE IN THE WORLD - a delicate creature only about knee-high to a person, with a TINY body, very thin fine legs like twigs, and an obviously miniature build. Enormous dark eyes with a dark tear-mark below each, a tuft of hair on the forehead, tiny straight spike horns, and a NORMAL SLIGHTLY POINTED MUZZLE - the nose is only very slightly elongated, absolutely NOT a trunk and NOT exaggerated. Its smallness is the whole point
baskingshark: A basking shark swimming in side profile with its mouth open, an enormous heavy grey-brown shark with a CONICAL POINTED SNOUT, an ENORMOUS ROUND GAPING MOUTH filled with pale feathery gill rakers and NO VISIBLE TEETH, and VAST GILL SLITS that wrap almost all the way around its head like collars. A large triangular dorsal fin, a strongly crescent-shaped tail, a bulky heavy body. A slow harmless filter feeder
goblinshark: A goblin shark swimming in side profile, a soft flabby PALE PINK deep-sea shark with a LONG FLAT BLADE-LIKE SNOUT projecting far forward above its mouth like a paddle, and its NAIL-LIKE NEEDLE-TOOTHED JAWS THRUST FORWARD AND OUTWARD from under that snout in a protruded bite. Small dark eyes, soft flabby body, small low fins, a long tail with a small lower lobe
frilledshark: A frilled shark swimming, a long dark brown EEL-LIKE shark with a slender serpentine snake-like body, a broad flattened head with a WIDE TERMINAL MOUTH across the very front of the snout, and SIX PAIRS OF RUFFLED FRILLY GILL SLITS with feathery frayed edges wrapped around its throat like collars. Small fins set far back near the tail, and a long eel-like tail
greenlandshark: A Greenland shark swimming in side profile, a massive sluggish heavy-bodied shark in dull grey-brown, with a THICK ROUNDED CYLINDRICAL BODY, a SHORT BLUNT ROUNDED SNOUT, very small eyes, small low rounded fins with no tall dorsal, and a broad heavy tail. Slow, soft and bulky, an old animal, not sleek or streamlined
epaulette: An epaulette shark resting on sand, a SMALL SLENDER shark with a BLUNT ROUNDED SNOUT and a long tapering body, pale cream-tan skin covered in SCATTERED DARK BROWN ROUND SPOTS, and a LARGE BLACK OVAL SPOT ringed in white sitting JUST BEHIND EACH PECTORAL FIN like a shoulder patch, which is the epaulette it is named for. Large paddle-shaped pectoral and pelvic fins that it walks on, two small dorsal fins set far back
oarfish: An oarfish, an IMMENSELY LONG RIBBON-SHAPED SILVER FISH, its body many times longer than it is deep and flattened like a strap, curving in loose waves. Silvery skin flecked with dark spots, a BRIGHT CRIMSON-RED DORSAL FIN OF SHORT RAYS RUNNING THE ENTIRE LENGTH OF ITS BACK from head to tail, a TALL CREST OF LONG RED PLUME-LIKE RAYS rising from the top of its head, and long trailing red oar-shaped pelvic fins. A small blunt head with a large dark eye
weedyseadragon: A weedy seadragon, a slender relative of the seahorse with a LONG STRAIGHT TUBULAR SNOUT, a thin elongated body ringed with bony bands, and a curled tail. Its body is reddish-orange crossed by PURPLE-BLUE BANDS and dotted with bright YELLOW SPOTS, and SMALL LEAF-SHAPED SKIN APPENDAGES sprout along its back, belly and tail. Held horizontally, drifting
boxjelly: A box jellyfish drifting, a TRANSLUCENT PALE BLUE JELLYFISH: a soft see-through gelatinous BELL shaped like a rounded cube with softly curved corners and a delicate membranous texture, and from each of its four lower corners hangs a BUNDLE OF MANY LONG FINE TRAILING TENTACLES streaming down and away. A soft translucent living sea creature, absolutely NOT a solid box, NOT a crate, NOT a container, NOT a hard-edged object
coconutcrab: A coconut crab, a GIGANTIC land crab, the largest in the world: a thick heavy domed carapace, EIGHT LONG IMMENSELY THICK POWERFUL WALKING LEGS spread wide and built to carry enormous weight, and TWO HEAVY CLAWS at the front with ONE MUCH LARGER THAN THE OTHER. Deep blue-purple and orange armour plating with a pebbled texture, small stalked eyes and short antennae. Massive, heavy-limbed and long-legged
harrishawk: A Harris's hawk perched on a branch, a dark chocolate-brown hawk with RICH CHESTNUT-RED SHOULDERS AND THIGHS, a yellow cere and yellow legs, a strongly hooked black beak and a fierce dark eye. It has EXACTLY ONE TAIL: a single dark tail with a BROAD WHITE BAND AT THE BASE AND A WHITE TIP, one tail only, no second tail anywhere
rattlesnake: A rattlesnake coiled ready to strike, a heavy-bodied pit viper with a broad triangular head, vertical pupils, and dark diamond blotches down a tan back. Its tail rises from the centre of the coil and the SEGMENTED RATTLE IS FIRMLY ATTACHED TO THE VERY TIP OF THAT TAIL, growing directly out of the tail as one continuous piece - a stack of pale horny interlocking buttons joined to the flesh, absolutely NOT floating, NOT detached, NOT separated by a gap
newt: A male great crested newt CRAWLING ON ALL FOUR LEGS along the ground, its BELLY LOW and its body HORIZONTAL, in side view - a lizard-like amphibian walking flat on the earth, absolutely NOT standing upright, NOT on its hind legs, NOT rearing up. Dark brown-black warty skin, a BRIGHT ORANGE BELLY WITH BOLD BLACK BLOTCHES visible along its lower flank, and a TALL JAGGED SAW-TOOTHED CREST running along its back and down its flattened tail
